clue.text: Capital performer in theatre has the intelligence to stimulate acting

parts.note: intelligence or brainpower is brain
'has' contracted is 's, giving S
to stimulate is to urge
an actor who is acting is on, i.e. on stage

explanation.surface: A star of the stage is praised for the brains that drive the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means head and 'theatre' is the operating theatre, so the performer works on heads. 'Has' is shortened to 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations in an operating theatre, and this one operates on the head, the capital at the top of the body.

clue.text: In this State well-to-do male finds no kicks

definitions.text: In this State well-to-do male finds no kicks

parts.note: a well is a bore, a hole drilled for water or oil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich man in this state finds no thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-to-do' looks like one word meaning wealthy; split it into well (BORE), to (a link) and do.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of finding no excitement, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Criminal outcome of Burns night?

parts.note: Burns Night, honouring the Scots poet Robert Burns, is reread as a night of things burning: a crime of setting fires

explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting property on fire is a crime, a night of burning caused on purpose.

clue.text: Account arranged by securing introduction to local inhabitant

indicators.note: one word securing another's introduction holds it inside

parts.note: a native is a local inhabitant
ARR is the abbreviation for arranged, as in music credits

explanation.surface: A report was put together by getting an introduction to a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it is just its abbreviation ARR. as printed on sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is a story or report, an account of events.

clue.text: University can upset one

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A university can upset a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one of something.

clue.text: Twisted thread for example drawn together

indicators.note: twisted thread is wound out of shape, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A twisted thread, for instance, is pulled together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' acts on the letters of 'thread' together with EG, giving GATHERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric gathered by a thread is drawn together into folds, and people gathered are brought together.

clue.text: It concerns the viewer or the listener when the programme head is involved

indicators.note: a letter that is involved is taken into the middle of the word

parts.note: otic means relating to the ear, the organ that does the listening

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something matters to viewers or listeners when the programme's boss gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' and 'listener' suggest TV and radio audiences, but they are the eye and the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye or sight, the organ that does the viewing.

clue.text: Climber knew a wind was getting up

parts.note: wist is an archaic word meaning knew

indicators.note: in a down clue a word getting up rises, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: air can mean a breeze or a wind

explanation.surface: A mountaineer sensed that the wind was rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant, the wisteria in an older spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering vine scrambles up walls, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: A way to get fish off the line

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An angler's method for getting a fish off the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the line' suggests a fishing line, but it means off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes astray wanders from its proper path, straying off the line it should follow.

clue.text: Check column carried in balance

indicators.note: one thing carried in another sits inside it, so the column goes within the balance

parts.note: the balance is what is left over, the rest
a column of vehicles or people on the move is a train

explanation.surface: An accountant checks a figure carried over in the balance sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back, and holding back is restraint.

clue.text: Follows tips

definitions.meaning: to follow someone secretly is to shadow or trail them
the tips or rear ends of things, such as the end of a coat or a coin's reverse side

explanation.definitionFit: A detective tails a suspect by following, and the tail is the hindmost tip of something.

clue.text: Refusal to include Ulster in trade

indicators.note: one word made to include another holds it inside

parts.note: a trade or bargain is a deal
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Ulster is excluded from a trade agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal, as in the denial of a request.

clue.text: Famous projectionist starts to make essential recommendations to troubled actor

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters
a troubled thing is disturbed, so the letters of actor are stirred up

explanation.surface: A cinema projectionist starts giving advice to a struggling actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'projectionist' is not a cinema worker: Gerardus Mercator devised the famous Mercator map projection. MER comes first, then CATOR from rearranging 'actor'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century Flemish cartographer gave his name to a widely used way of projecting the globe onto a flat map.

clue.text: Magical flier?

parts.note: read as a falcon that is also the wizard of Arthurian legend: a small bird of prey shares its name with King Arthur's magician

explanation.definitionFit: A small falcon shares its name with the wizard of King Arthur's court, so the bird is a flier with a magical name.

clue.text: Old bag's name coming up in decree

indicators.note: the reversed name sits in the decree, between its letters

parts.note: a decree is a rule

indicators.note: in a down clue something coming up rises, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to name, as when citing a source

explanation.surface: An old hag's name surfaces in a court decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bag' reads as an insult, but it is an old-fashioned drawstring handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule was a small woman's handbag of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Injured greylag following barnacles' leader to base

indicators.note: one piece following another comes after it
the leader of a word is its first letter
an injured bird is damaged, so the letters of greylag are mangled

explanation.surface: A wounded goose follows a barnacle goose back to its base.
explanation.walkthrough: Greylag and barnacle are both species of goose, which makes 'base' look like a home rather than the definition meaning mean or poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Base can mean mean-spirited or wretched, and beggarly describes something mean, paltry or contemptible.

clue.text: Boatman who is doomed to go about turbulent lido

indicators.note: one word put about another surrounds it

parts.note: someone doomed is a goner, one about to go

indicators.note: turbulent means churning, so the letters of lido are stirred

explanation.surface: A boatman is doomed to cross a stormy lido.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who is doomed to go' is one phrase for a single piece, and 'turbulent' is the anagram signal acting on 'lido', not a description of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola on the canals of Venice, so he is a boatman.

clue.text: Strips of record in competitions

indicators.note: the record goes in the competitions, between their letters

parts.note: a drive is an organised competition, as in a whist drive
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Bits of vinyl are handed out in competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: A whist drive is a British social card competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone is to strip them of something they have.

clue.text: Material given to journalist was significant

parts.note: material or substance is matter
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Information passed to a reporter turned out to be important.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was significant counted for something, which is to say it had importance.

clue.text: Little to be extracted from Rome agreement

indicators.note: the letters are to be extracted from a run within the printed words

explanation.surface: Little was gained from a treaty signed in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or small in amount, so it is a synonym of little.

clue.text: Number covered by American assistance is left to the imagination

indicators.note: a piece covered by another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: assistance is aid

explanation.surface: A figure hidden under US aid spending is left for people to guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fits the phrase 'what is unsaid', a thing left unspoken and so left to the imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: What goes unspoken is never stated, so the listener must imagine it.

clue.text: Contest to be conclusive, on his say-so

definitions.meaning: a final match played to settle a tied result
a person whose word settles the issue, the one who makes the decision

explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game settles a tie, and a person who settles a matter is the one who decides it.

clue.text: Provide equipment for expert around squash court

indicators.note: a word placed around another encloses it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: squashed letters are crushed out of shape, so the letters of court are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kit out a top player for the squash court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash court' looks like a single sports venue, but 'squash' is the anagram signal acting on 'court', and 'around' puts the expert's letters on either side of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre someone is to equip or outfit them, typically with military gear.

clue.text: Express with no reservation available

definitions.meaning: to express something in words is to say or voice it
complete or absolute, without any holding back

explanation.definitionFit: To voice words is to speak them, and an absolute or total thing is complete without reservation.

clue.text: Infinite jester round the bend

indicators.note: one piece placed round another surrounds it

parts.note: a jester is a comic
an S-bend is a bend shaped like that letter, giving S

explanation.surface: A court fool has gone completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' suggests a jester gone crazy, but 'round' is the container signal and 'the bend' gives S, as in an S-bend in a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic means vast beyond measure, as boundless as the universe itself.

clue.text: Sudanese warrior had tumble in the road

indicators.note: the tumbled letters go in the road, between its letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: letters that tumble fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A Sudanese fighter took a fall on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahdi led a revolt in Sudan in the 1880s, defeating General Gordon at Khartoum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mahdi was the nineteenth-century Sudanese religious leader whose forces fought British-led armies.

clue.text: . Dig up some food

definitions.meaning: to ... up roots is to dig them out of the ground
slang for food or a meal

explanation.definitionFit: To grub is to dig in the soil, and grub is also informal slang for food.

clue.text: Soldiers fired and fired again

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps of soldiers
fired in the sense of set alight is lit

explanation.surface: Troops shot and then shot once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests guns, but here it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set alight once more has been kindled a second time.

clue.text: Suddenly went right inside and put on a coat

indicators.note: a letter going inside a word is placed within it

parts.note: to go suddenly out of sight is to vanish

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly went in and then pulled on a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on a coat' suggests dressing, but the coat is a layer of paint or lacquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is applied as a coat of glossy finish over wood.

clue.text: Fence keeps reckless dramatist in credit

indicators.note: the reckless dramatist sits in the credit abbreviation, between its letters

parts.note: reckless means rash
J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan, was a Scottish dramatist

explanation.surface: A rash playwright is fenced off while still in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside safety barrier is a kind of fence put up to stop vehicles leaving the road.
